stories.title: US investigates Singapore firm Megaspeed over alleged Nvidia chip exports to China
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice and Department of Commerce announced a joint investigation into Singapore‑based Megaspeed, accusing it of violating U.S. export controls by facilitating shipments of Nvidia’s high‑end AI chips to China. The probe, which began in 2024, follows concerns that such chips may have reached China despite restrictions. U.S. authorities also suspect former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang of spying for Beijing, a claim China denies, and note that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned after personal scandal revelations.

stories.title: Ukraine damages Crimean Bridge, section collapses into water
stories.summary: Ukraine has severely damaged the Crimean Bridge that links Russia to occupied Crimea, with images showing a section of the structure collapsed into the water. President Volodymyr Zelensky described the strike as an unprecedented operation. In Kyiv, Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said traffic on the Pivnichnyi and Pivdennyi bridges over the Dnipro River had partially resumed after overnight Russian attacks.
stories.why: The damage hampers a major supply route for Russian forces and has symbolic significance in the conflict.

stories.title: UK sanctions eight firms over West Bank settlement construction
stories.summary: The UK has sanctioned eight construction and property development firms it says are involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank, the first package of measures since the government announced a tougher approach to Israeli actions in the territory. The government said the sanctions would disrupt the firms' flows of finance and their ability to support building in the West Bank. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar called the sanctions a "hostile act targeting private, law-abiding companies".
stories.why: The measures aim to cut financing and construction support for settlements the UK says are illegal under international law, at a time when settlement construction has risen sharply and settler attacks have surged.

stories.title: Canadian home sales edge up 0.3% in October, still 10.6% below October 2025
stories.summary: National home sales rose 0.3 percent month‑over‑month in October, according to the Canadian Real Estate Association, beating some analysts’ expectations. Despite the gain, sales were 10.6 percent lower than in October 2025, reflecting a market that remains flat amid recent interest‑rate hikes and a sluggish economy.
stories.why: The figures show that higher rates and current economic conditions continue to suppress housing activity.

stories.title: Indian government bond yields fall as oil prices drop
stories.summary: In early trading, Indian government bonds rose after crude oil prices fell sharply. The yield on the benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond slipped to 7.2813%, reflecting reduced inflationary pressure and lower concerns about aggressive RBI rate hikes. Analysts noted that the lower oil price also supported the rupee and helped narrow the current‑account deficit.
stories.why: RBI action or currency-market developments can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.

stories.title: India’s current account deficit projected at 1.2% of GDP in FY27
stories.summary: Union Bank of India projects the current account deficit to reach about 1.2% of GDP in the 2026‑27 fiscal year, citing higher crude oil prices and strong gold demand as drivers. The merchandise trade deficit widened to $39.88 billion in October as imports rose, while the services trade surplus was almost unchanged.

stories.title: India’s retail inflation rises to 6.09% in October 2026
stories.summary: India’s retail inflation breached the RBI’s 6 % tolerance ceiling, reaching 6.09 % in October 2026. Food prices were surging, putting pressure on household budgets, and the central bank faced questions about whether it had acted too late on interest rates and why its inflation forecasts missed the mark.

stories.title: Google says Gmail is operating normally amid outage rumors
stories.summary: On Tuesday, Google posted on X that it sees no evidence of a broad Gmail service disruption and directed users to the Gmail real‑time status dashboard. The statement was made after reports of a Gmail outage circulated on X at the same time Apple experienced confirmed outages. The rumors originated from a Downdetector post, which is a crowdsourced, non‑official source.
stories.why: Users should rely on Google’s official status page rather than crowdsourced sites when checking service health.
